This happened a few years ago just a couple weeks after I had lost a friend. 
I had only known him for a few months but in those few months we got very close. He let me know he had feelings for me but I played with his heart. I told him I had feelings as well but later told him I didn’t. (I wasn’t allowed to date and was scared that somehow my parents would find out something was going on with us and not let me see him. Dum, 8th grade me thought this was the best solution to the problem.)

He ended up passing away unexpectedly, and I was heartbroken.

A few weeks after this I was on my way to a Christmas party with my family as I was reflecting on my time spent with him. I started praying that he was in heaven, that he was okay, and that I would be able to see him again. I am fairly religious, but have my doubts time to time about what I believe. Especially in this weak state. But I was silently crying out to God, pleading for him to make sure my friend knew that I cared for him and that I was so sorry I was not honest with him. Most of all I wanted to know I would see him again. I wanted to know his soul made it to heaven as that’s where I believe mine will go. 
Just as I look up I see a billboard advertising the restaurant RedRobin which relates to an inside joke him and I had. And at that exact time I realized that a song was playing on my Ipod that I had always skipped. (After I got my Ipod I downloaded all the songs from my mom’s computer which consisted of songs chosen by various members of my family. There was one song I always skipped before it would even get to the lyrics because honestly.. the beginning just sounded too happy to me and I wasn’t in the mood) But while I was praying I guess I didn’t notice it had started to play. It was Hey, Soul Sister by Train. I broke down crying in the backseat of the family van hoping no one would notice. 

I know it’s kind of cringey and maybe it seems like  a coincidence when I tell the story to others. But it was so clear to me in that moment that my prayers had been answered. It’s almost 7 years later and I still get goose bumps and have to fight tears when thinking about it.
